newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA CRUMBLE TO MCGRATH AND GILLSEPIE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA CRUMBLE TO MCGRATH AND GILLSEPIE.

text.p: Fast bowlers Glenn McGrath and Jason Gillespie grabbed an early brace of wickets each as South Africa collapsed to 64 for four at lunch on the first day of the second test in Port Elizabeth on Friday.

Australian captain Mark Taylor's decision to bowl first was immediately vindicated on a green, moist wicket when opener Gary Kirsten could only fend a Gillespie lifter into the hands of Matthew Hayden for a duck in the sixth over of the innings.
Jacques Kallis also failed to trouble the scorers. Another Gillespie lifter saw him lob a simple catch to Greg Blewett at backward short leg.
Opener Adam Bacher survived an impassioned appeal for a catch at the wicket before he had scored but then fell to McGrath for 11, caught in the gully by Matthew Elliott.

With wickets falling at 13, 17 and 21, a grim faced South African captain Hansie Cronje strode to the wicket but his determination amounted to nothing -- literally. He became the third duck when he was bowled off an inside edge by McGrath to leave his team on 22 for four.

The fightback began with a cover drive for four by Daryll Cullinan off Gillespie but there was more drama when the batsman appeared to rule himself not out when apparently 'caught' by Hayden at short leg.

Cullinan pulled a short ball from McGrath straight at Hayden who amazingly emerged from his crouched position with the ball in his hands. But Cullinan indicated that the ball had lodged itself in the fielder's helmet from where Hayden had retrieved it.
The umpires conferred and finally ruled the batsman not out. At lunch Cullinan was 28 not out with Herschelle Gibbs on 13.
